acceptanceMaintenance.action: Added the tests requested by the review pass, and then a PSL/PSQ case during the signing session itself. Every requirement fingerprint covers the whole evidence set, so each of those additions moved all 95 entries, including decisions already recorded by hand.
acceptanceMaintenance.carriedForwardDuringSigning: R29, R92, R31, R46 and R89 were recorded before the PSL/PSQ case was added. Their requirement text, cases, fixtures, queries and expected answers are untouched by that addition, so each keeps its reviewer, date and rationale verbatim and only its fingerprint moved.
acceptanceMaintenance.refreshRationale: These requirements' text, cases, fixtures, queries and expected answers are byte-identical to the ones already accepted; only the shared evidence digest moved, because new fixtures and queries entered the hash set. The recorded acceptance is carried over unchanged.
acceptanceMaintenance.versionBump: Release stamps no longer re-open a review. assess.py blanks owl:versionInfo and owl:versionIRI values before hashing an ontology module, so bumping the release version leaves the evidence digest unchanged; every other byte of those files still counts. The 2.1.1 bump was the last one to move fingerprints, and it moved them only because the hashing change itself is in a hashed script.
acceptanceMaintenance.withdrawnRationale: These gained new cases, fixtures or corrected interpretations, so the earlier acceptance no longer covers what they now assert. R83 was accepted on 10 September as unassessed and has since gained its first case, which is exactly the condition that acceptance was conditional on. They are listed in generated/review-queue.json and need a fresh decision; the acceptance they carried is kept verbatim under supersededAcceptance for comparison.

R27.rationale: Read the LAA definition at VCFv4.5.tex:686-694 and the equivalence table at 703-710. The eight expected rows follow each Number=LR value to the global allele its local position names; at POS 1 LAA=2,4 skips ALT alleles A and T, so the mapping is genuinely non-identity, unlike the pre-existing case whose LAA=1,2 makes it the identity. POS 4's empty LAA is the REF-only case. Corrected GT from the printed 2/4 to 2/2: GT is Number=1 and not a local-allele field, LPL is minimal at local C/C and the global PL at index 5 = 2/2, and row 2 prints 0/3 in both of its rows; reported as samtools/hts-specs#871. Full local-to-global equivalence is covered separately by R83. Condensed structure fails as the documented profile design choice.

R45.rationale: Accepted as unassessed for all three applicable versions. The gVCF tables at VCFv4.3.tex:1440-1446 and VCFv4.5.tex:1867-1873 need four corrections before they can serve as an oracle - FORMAT 'P' reading as 'PL', ';' before each LEN reading as ':', the inclusive LEN values 5, 5 and 20 where 4, 4 and 19 are printed, and the 4396 variant row dropping the MIN_DP and LEN keys it cannot use - and those corrections are disputed upstream in samtools/hts-specs#868 (https://github.com/samtools/hts-specs/issues/868). Tests were drafted on this reviewer's reading and deliberately withdrawn rather than baked in: if the specification resolves #868 differently the expected answers would be wrong. Register them once that issue closes. <NON_REF> aliasing and the LEN-from-END fallback are untested for the same reason.

R46.rationale: Read the worked example at VCFv4.5.tex:1969-1971 and the Figure 11 prose at 1932-1937. The specification's two non-symbolic rows omit the mandatory INFO column, so the fixture supplies '.'; that erratum is reported upstream in samtools/hts-specs#870 (https://github.com/samtools/hts-specs/issues/870) alongside the Figure 11 exponent. RUB's separate partitioning by RUC remains untested under R88.

GT:M5mC:M5hmC 0|0:0.9,0:0,0.1' (two phased C copies, two values per field); and 'chr 40 C A,T,G,ACG GT:M5mC /3|1/0|4|0/0/3/1:0.25,0.1,0.5,0.6,.' where GT is octoploid with allele values 0, 1, 3 and 4, all within the four-allele ALT list, and per-allele contributions in GT order with unphased aggregation at first occurrence give G->1, A->0, C->1, ACG->2, phased C->1 and nothing for the three repeats, i.e. five values. 4.5:1846-1880.note: Reviewer decision. (1) Separators: the ';' before each LEN value must be ':'. Semicolon is the INFO separator, whereas sample sub-fields are colon-delimited against the FORMAT key list, so the first row reads '0/0:25:60:23:0,60,900:14'. (2) LEN is the inclusive block length, so END = POS + LEN - 1. The reserved definition is 'length of the <*> reference block for this sample' and END is defined as the end position calculated from FORMAT LEN. The row POS=4390, END=4390, LEN=1 is decisive, since END-POS would give a block length of zero, and POS=4370, END=4383, LEN=14 confirms it. Corrected LEN values: 4370->14 (as printed), 4384-4388->5 (printed 4), 4390->1 (as printed), 4391-4395->5 (printed 4), 4397-4416->20 (printed 19). (3) Additional erratum found during this review: the row '1 4396 . G C,<*> ... GT:DP:GQ:MIN_DP:PL:LEN 0/0:24:52:0,52,95,66,95,97' is a variant row with no reference block, so MIN_DP and LEN do not apply and the four supplied sub-fields make MIN_DP absorb the PL vector; the uniform FORMAT string was applied to every row of the table without adjusting this one. Its corrected FORMAT is GT:DP:GQ:PL. The existing gvcf-v4.5.vcf fixture and queries/r30-decode.rq already implement END = POS + LEN - 1 and are correct under this decision.

4.5:1917-2047.note: Reviewer decision. (1) Obsolete key names: RS, RL and RC are typos for RUS, RUL and RUC; the corrected overview list is 'RN, RUS, RUL, RUC, RB and RUB'. (2) The figure sequence CAGCAGCAGTTGTTG is (CAG)3(TTG)2, not (CAG)4(TTG)2 - it contains three CAG units and is fifteen bases. Corrected figure values: RN=2,1; RUS=CAG,TTG,CA; RUL=3,3,2; RUC=3,2,3; RB=9,6,6, with the second allele CACACA = (CA)3. (3) RUL/RUB nesting: RUB is partitioned by RUC (one value per repeat unit) while RUS, RUL, RUC and RB are partitioned by RN (one value per repeat sequence). (4) The main worked example is internally consistent and usable as an oracle - verified arithmetically: reference (CAG)10 at 101-130 (30 bases, SVLEN=30, POS=100 padding); allele 1 (CAG)30 = 90 bases with RN=1, RB=90 and INFO CN=90/30=3; allele 2 (CAG)5(CA)(CAG)4 = 29 bases with RN=3, RUS=CAG,CA,CAG, RB=15,2,12 and INFO CN=29/30; the flattened RUS is CAG,CAG,CA,CAG and RB is 90,15,2,12 exactly as printed; FORMAT CN=(90+29)/30. The phased non-symbolic rows also check out: 'chr1 117 AG A' deletes the G of the sixth CAG unit (116-118) on haplotype 2 (GT=0|1) and 'chr1 130 G G+20xCAG' adds twenty units on haplotype 1 (GT=1|0), matching GT=1|2 on the summary record. Printed CN values are truncated rather than rounded (0.9666 and 3.9666 for 0.96667 and 3.96667). The CIRUC example is likewise consistent (65x3/30 = 6.5). (5) Additional erratum found during this review: the RUB example 'chr1 1000000 . T <CNV:TR> . . SVLEN=20000;CN=1.25;RUL=10000;RUC=5;RUB=10000,10500,11000,11500,12000' is arithmetically inconsistent - CN must be sample allelic length divided by reference allelic length, and sum(RUB)=55000 gives 2.75 while RUL*RUC=50000 gives 2.5, neither of which is 1.25. Excluded as a CN oracle; still usable for RUB cardinality (five values = RUC) and the variable-unit-length capability. (6) Additional erratum, 4.4 only: the same record carries END=20000 at POS=1000000, i.e. END < POS; END should be POS+SVLEN = 1020000. Removed in 4.5 with the deprecation of INFO END.

4.5:2726-2739.note: Reviewer decision. (1) Number=P was introduced in VCF 4.4, not 4.5. The pinned 4.4 text defines P in the FORMAT Number list, gives PSL and PSO Number=P in the reserved genotype table, and records it in the 4.4 errata; the 4.5 entry 'Added Number=P support ...' is inaccurate as a 4.4-to-4.5 delta, and what 4.5 actually adds is the new M Number and the local-allele Numbers alongside it. Number=P is therefore in scope for both 4.4 and 4.5, and R82 already lists both versions. (2) Modification key syntax: the changelog's 'FORMAT keys of the form M[0-9]+' is incomplete. The main text reserves M[0-9]+[ACGTUN], and equally DPM[0-9]+[ACGTUN] and ADM[0-9]+[ACGTUN]; the trailing base letter is required and defines the base the modification occurs on, with U synonymous with T. The full three-family form governs, and declarations.json already records all three patterns.

4.5:2740-2745.note: Reviewer decision: the main text governs - P is a Number, not a Type. The FORMAT section lists P among the additional Number possibilities ('P: The field has one value for each allele value defined in GT'), the reserved genotype table gives PSL, PSO and PSQ Number=P with Types String, Integer and Integer, and the enumerated FORMAT Types are only Integer, Float, Character and String, so Type=P is not well formed. The VCF 4.5 changelog independently writes 'Added Number=P support', corroborating the correction. The erratum should read 'Number=P added to the FORMAT Number list'. Mandatory-attribute and cardinality expectations are unaffected.

4.5:2746-2773.note: Reviewer decision: the main text governs. ID, Number, Type and Description are required for both ##INFO and ##FORMAT lines in 4.4 and 4.5 - 'FORMAT meta-information lines are structured lines with required fields ID, Number, Type, and Description' is as explicit as the INFO sentence. The changelog entry 'Number, Type and Description required only for INFO meta-information lines' omits FORMAT and is a drafting error. What actually changed relative to 4.3 is that Number, Type and Description are not required for the other spec-defined structured lines (FILTER, ALT, contig, META, SAMPLE, PEDIGREE) nor for undefined structured lines, where only ID is required. R03 (INFO declarations) and R52 (FORMAT declarations) are both correctly scoped and need no change.

4.5:497-812.note:
Reviewer decision: the PSL illustration is not usable as an oracle; the PSO illustration is. PSL table defects: row 2 ('chr20 10 . A T,G ... GT=|1/2|3') uses allele index 3 although ALT lists only two alleles, and row 3 ('chr20 15 . G C ... GT=1|2') uses index 2 although ALT lists one; row 3 is additionally self-contradictory, because with the leading indicator omitted and no '/' present VCF 4.4/4.5 make the first indicator implicitly '|' (phased), yet PSL='.,chr20*10*1' marks that allele unphased; and ploidy is inconsistent between rows 2 (three alleles) and 3 (two) for the same sample on the same CHROM. A corrected, internally consistent equivalent preserving the illustrative content is: 'chr19 5 . T G . PASS DP=100 GT:PSL |0/1:chr19*5*1,.' (unchanged); 'chr20 10 . A T,G . PASS DP=100 GT:PSL |1/2|0:chr20*10*1,.,chr19*5*1'; 'chr20 15 . G C . PASS DP=100 GT:PSL /0/0|1:.,.,chr20*10*1'. Any test built on it must be labelled reviewer-authored, not spec-verbatim. PSO: the example is internally consistent and supplies a usable per-allele oracle - chr1:10 <DUP> GT allele 3 -> PSL chr1*10*3, PSO 3; chr1:20 allele 3 (REF A) -> chr1*10*1, PSO 4 and allele 4 (ALT G) -> chr1*10*3, PSO 1; chr1:30 allele 3 (REF G) -> chr1*10*1, PSO 2 and allele 4 (ALT T) -> chr1*10*3, PSO 5. Ordinals 1-5 occur exactly once each and give one total traversal order of the derivative chromosome: ALT G at chr1:20 (1), REF at chr1:30 (2), the duplication junction (3), REF at chr1:20 (4), ALT T at chr1:30 (5) - exactly the stated reading that the first SNV lies on the first copy of the duplicated region and the second on the second copy. The rise from three to four allele values inside the duplicated interval is intended, not an error. Request an R82 case on that basis: expose per sample-allele the PSL name and PSO ordinal and recover the total order.

Reviewer decision: GT=2/2 is correct and the local-allele row's GT=2/4 is the typo. GT is Number=1, Type=String and is not a local-allele field, so it carries global allele indices in both rows - confirmed by row 2 of the same table, where both rows print 0/3. With LAA=2,4 the local alleles are [G(REF), C, <*>] and LPL=90,80,0,100,110,120 is minimal (0) at local genotype 1/1 = C/C, while the global PL list is minimal (0) at index 5 = genotype 2/2 = C/C; every other value maps consistently (local 00/01/02/12/22 to global 00/02/04/24/44 = 90/80/100/110/120) and LAD=20,30,10 matches AD=20,.,30,.,10. Rows 2-4 were verified the same way and are correct as printed. The MXaoN/MxaoN capitalisation question is resolved in the base modification section: the reserved-key table form MXaoN governs. The PSL/PSO questions are resolved separately in this same section's note above.

4.5:824-840.note: Reviewer decision: adopt the error-probability interpretation. The Q-suffix sentence is internally inconsistent - it calls the quantity a 'log-complementary ... posterior probability' but prints -10 log10 Pr(Data|Model), which is neither complementary nor posterior. The normative per-key definitions in the same document govern: GQ is '-10log10 p(genotype call is wrong, conditioned on the site's being variant)' and CNQ is '-10log10 p(copy number genotype call is wrong)'. So a Q-suffixed value is -10 log10 (1 - Pr(Model|Data)), the phred-scaled probability that the reported call is wrong; the printed formula drops the complement and inverts the conditioning. Assessment impact: none. This settles the field's stated meaning, which the vocabulary carries through the reserved definition and the declaration Description; no expected answer in any registered case depends on the numeric semantics, and R69 keeps its scale-distinction scope unchanged.

4.5:841-1141.note: Reviewer decision: RS, RL and RC are typos for RUS, RUL and RUC. No key named RC, RS or RL is declared anywhere in 4.4 or 4.5; the declared repeat keys are RN, RUS, RUL, RUC, RB, RUB, CIRUC and CIRB, and there are exactly three affected sentences per version (VCFv4.4.tex lines 973, 1759, 1827; VCFv4.5.tex lines 1134, 1928, 1995). The overview's field list 'RN, RS, RL, RB, RC and RUL' both mis-spells three names and repeats RUL; corrected it reads 'RN, RUS, RUL, RUC, RB and RUB'. With that substitution the examples are usable as an oracle. The same correction settles the RUB nesting question: the sentence 'a list for each RC entry, the length of which is determined by the corresponding integer RUC value' means RUB is partitioned by RUC (one value per repeat unit), whereas RUS, RUL, RUC and RB are partitioned by RN (one value per repeat sequence) - two different flattening rules in the same record.
